newsitem.title: USA: Clinton may give surgeon general job dual role.
newsitem.headline: Clinton may give surgeon general job dual role.

text.p: Dr. David Satcher, director of the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, is the leading candidate to become the next U.S. surgeon general, a White House official said on Saturday.

The White House was considering combining the job of surgeon general with the assistant secretary at the Health and Human Services Department and nominating Satcher for both, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
"He's very much the leading candidate and the administration is looking at the possibility of having him serve in both positions," the official said.
The jobs had been combined under President Jimmy Carter but were divided by President Ronald Reagan when he took office.
Satcher, 56, is a former president of Meharry Medical College in Nashville, Tennessee, and had been a candidate for the surgeon general's position in 1995.
The surgeon general's job, essentially the government's chief spokesman for Americans' health and wellness, has been a constant headache for President Clinton.
His first surgeon general, Joycelyn Elders, was forced to resign after an uproar developed over her remarks about sex education, condoms and masturbation.
Then Clinton nominated Dr. Henry Foster for the job, only to withdraw the nomination after it became clear Foster had performed more abortions than he had originally admitted.
The acting surgeon general, Dr. Audrey Manley, is leaving the position July 1 to head Spelman College in Atlanta.
